claims.text: Retention of toughness in high-entropy alloys is governed by the formation and stability of an optimal distribution of metastable nanoscale precipitates.
A controlled heat-treatment regimen can tailor the fraction, size, and spatial distribution of the metastable precipitates.
Metastable tetragonal ZrO2 particles in (WTaNbZrTi)C transform under mechanical loading.
The load-induced ZrO2 transformation is specifically a tetragonal-to-monoclinic transformation.
Transformation of the metastable particles produces stress fields that shield the crack tip.
The precipitate transformation promotes crack deflection, crack bridging, and crack branching.
Microcracking associated with the metastable-particle microstructure contributes to toughening.
Particle size and location affect susceptibility to transformation and therefore the toughening response.
Precipitate volume fraction is a governing mediator of transformation-induced toughness in this material.
The baseline material is as-cast or conventionally processed and has an unoptimized, random precipitate distribution.
An optimized heat treatment will increase fracture toughness by approximately 1 MPa·m^(1/2) or more relative to the as-cast baseline.
The transformation-toughening contribution in the cited (WTaNbZrTi)C material is approximately 1.0 MPa·m^(1/2).
Heat treatments producing excessively coarse or unstable precipitate distributions will reduce toughness or leave it negligibly changed.
The proposed mechanism should hold for annealing temperatures from approximately 800°C to 1100°C with suitable dwell times.
The mechanism applies only within a defined compositional window.
The mechanism may cease to govern toughness when other microstructural processes or phase transformations dominate.
Failure of the heat treatment to change the precipitate population would falsify the mechanistic hypothesis.
If samples demonstrably possessing the optimized precipitate characteristics show no statistically significant toughness improvement over the control, the hypothesis is falsified.

contradictions.description: The proposal is framed as applying to high-entropy alloys, but its concrete example, (WTaNbZrTi)C with ZrO2 particles, is a high-entropy carbide ceramic rather than a metallic alloy.
